property_summary: supportsInterface(type(IERC1155MetadataURI).interfaceId) returns true for any state of the contract
supportsInterface returns true for the IERC1155 interface ID regardless of contract state
For any address and boolean, supportsInterface(type(IERC1155).interfaceId) returns true before and after adjustAdminAccess is called.
After adjustAdminAccess is called with any arguments, supportsInterface returns the same value as before the call for any interface ID.
After calling adjustAdminAccess with any arguments, supportsInterface returns true for the IERC1155 interface ID.
supportsInterface(interfaceId) returns true if interfaceId matches IERC1155 or IERC1155MetadataURI.
supportsInterface returns true for IERC165 interface ID
supportsInterface returns true when interfaceId is IERC1155's interfaceId.
supportsInterface returns true for the IERC1155MetadataURI interface ID
supportsInterface returns false for a non-existent interface ID that is not IERC165, IERC1155, or IERC1155MetadataURI.
After any call to adjustAdminAccess, the balanceOf function returns the actual balance from the internal mapping, not zero.
balanceOf returns actual balance for a non-zero address owner
For any address that is not the zero address, balanceOf returns a value that does not exceed the maximum representable uint256 (i.e., is never zero for an existing balance after a mint).
balanceOf returns the actual balance from the internal mapping for any non-zero account and any token id
balanceOf returns the sum of all minted amounts for a given account and token id, after any admin change.
After adjusting admin access for any address, the balanceOf for that address with id 0 should remain the same as the id-specific balance before and after the call.
Fuzz: adjustAdminAccess does not change the balanceOf result for any address and any token id.
The balanceOf function returns the ERC1155 token balance, not the native ETH balance.
After adjusting admin access, the balanceOf function must return the same value as querying an ERC1155 balance mapping would, or revert gracefully (not return ETH balance).

For any account and id, balanceOf(account, id) must return a value less than or equal to 2^128, because ERC1155 balances are stored in uint256 mapping but should be bounded, while account.balance can exceed that.
balanceOfBatch always returns a uint256 array of the same length as the accounts array, where each element equals balanceOf(accounts[i], ids[i]) for the corresponding index i.
The length of the returned batchBalances array equals the length of the accounts input array.
After adjustAdminAccess, balanceOfBatch returns the correct length and values for any pair of equal-length arrays.
After adjustAdminAccess, the length of balanceOfBatch result equals accounts.length for any pair of arrays.
balanceOfBatch returns an array whose length equals accounts.length for any accounts and ids of equal lengths.
For any arrays accounts and ids, the length of balanceOfBatch is always less than the maximum of the two input lengths, which fails when lengths differ
BalanceOfBatch returns an array whose length equals the length of accounts for any input arrays with equal lengths, and reverts for unequal lengths.
For any valid input arrays of accounts and ids, balanceOfBatch returns an array whose length equals accounts.length
The balanceOfBatch function returns correct balance for every second account, skipping odd-indexed accounts.

For consecutive odd-indexed entries, the cumulative balance from balanceOfBatch at even indices equals the sum of balances from balanceOfBatch at preceding even indices plus the queried odd-indexed balances individually.
For any valid arrays of accounts and ids of equal length, the balance returned by balanceOfBatch at each index is the same as the balance returned by balanceOf for that account and id.
For any valid input arrays of accounts and ids, balanceOfBatch returns an array whose length equals accounts.length
The balanceOfBatch function should return the correct balances for all accounts starting from index 0, not skipping the first element.
After calling adjustAdminAccess, balanceOfBatch returns arrays with the same length as accounts input.
The balanceOfBatch function returns arrays where the first element balances[0] equals the result of calling balanceOf(accounts[0], ids[0]) directly.
After adjusting admin access, the balanceOfBatch function returns arrays where the length equals the accounts array length and index-0 element is correctly set.
For any accounts and ids arrays with equal length, balanceOfBatch returns an array whose length equals the accounts length.
balanceOfBatch returns an array whose length equals the input accounts array length
Sending an empty array to balanceOfBatch does not exceed the array length.
After adjustAdminAccess sets isAdmin for an address to false, the isApprovedForAll function returns false for that address as operator.
After setting an address as admin via adjustAdminAccess, isApprovedForAll returns true for that address as operator on the default admin role holder's account.
After adjusting admin access for an address, isApprovedForAll returns false for a non-approved operator.
After adjustAdminAccess, allowanceRemaining for any tokenId is always at least the dailyAllowance or the previous value (i.e., never decreases unexpectedly).

After adjustAdminAccess, the allowanceRemaining for any address and tokenId is always exactly the value it had before the call, because the public function does not change any internal state related to allowances.

After adjustAdminAccess, the allowanceRemaining for the caller and any tokenId is always equal to the dailyAllowance of that tokenId, because the daily allowance replenish time is set to the future, so the getAllowanceRemaining function returns the dailyAllowance.

After adjustAdminAccess, the allowanceRemaining for the caller and any tokenId is never decreased relative to the value returned by getAllowanceRemaining before the call, because the function does not modify allowances.
After adjustAdminAccess, getAllowanceRemaining for any address and tokenId remains unchanged from before the call.
